subject: Dedicated capacity: tailored ramping options and minimum guarantees for Sentinel Health
messages:
From: Caroline Doe <caroline@sentinelhealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing + ramp cadence

Hey Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Sentinel is excited about the latency profile on the Retriever model. Our procurement and Eng leads asked for a concrete set of reservation options we can include in an internal business case. Key asks:

- Concrete cluster sizes (min GPUs per lane / total pool) for pilots and production, with example throughput assumptions.
- A staged ramp plan tied to quarterly milestones (we'd prefer a path that minimizes immediate commit but protects our SLA).
- Min guaranteed GPUs and warm-up/activation windows (we need an idea of cold-start risk).
- Rough price ranges for each option so we can compare to on-prem alternatives.

Could you send two alternatives: a low-commit pilot-first option and a 12-month runway plan with staged activation? We have a budget review next Thursday. I've attached a one-page SOW draft.

Thanks,
Caroline
Caroline Doe
Head of Product
Sentinel Health
Attachments: Sentinel_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Doe <caroline@sentinelhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing + ramp cadence

Caroline — appreciate the clarity. Attached is a worksheet with option-level numbers (redwood-dedicated-offer-worksheet.xlsx) and a short capacity CSV. High level, two pragmatic paths we recommend:

Option 1 — Pilot-first, low up-front commit (Pilot Lane + Production on demand)- Minimum committed: 8xA100-equivalent GPUs (pilot lane)- Production fallback: hosted burst to managed pool until commit triggers- Timeline: 1 month pilot -> decision point -> 0-6 month gradual commit- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 qps (small gen) / ~40k tokens/min- Pros: low immediate spend, fast time-to-validate- Cons: contention risk during peak without burst credits

Option 2 — Staggered reservation runway (12-month, predictable)- Phase A (Months 0-3): 12 committed GPUs (warm lane) + 6 on-demand- Phase B (Months 4-8): increase to 24 committed GPUs- Phase C (Months 9-12): 36 committed GPUs (full production)- Release plan: weekly ramp gates with automated canary routing; automatic fallback to smaller model if capacity constrained- Expected steady-state throughput at Month 12: ~900 qps / ~180k tokens/min- Pros: predictable latency and cost per token; SLA-backed latency targets- Cons: higher committed spend up front vs Option 1

Minimum guarantees we suggest for Sentinel given your latency SLO (95th < 300ms): 12 GPUs to keep warm-lane coverage and <2% request queuing under expected traffic variance. Karthik, I've looped you for technical confirmation on batching assumptions and warm-start timing.

Next steps: 1) Karthik to confirm throughput mappings and min_gpus guardrail, 2) Marissa to provide pricing tiers and ramp credits, 3) we prepare a short PO/term sheet for your review.

Best,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-offer-worksheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), capacity-estimates.csv (text/csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Caroline Doe <caroline@sentinelhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing + ramp cadence

On Fri, Oct 16, 2026 at 11:03 AM Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Minimum guarantees we suggest for Sentinel given your latency SLO (95th < 300ms): 12 GPUs to keep warm-lane coverage and <2% request queuing under expected traffic variance.

Confirming the assumptions behind the numbers above so procurement can tie to expected QPS:

Assumptions: 
- Model: 13B decoder-only, 4k context, optimized kernels (A100-class perf)
- Average token generation per request: 120 tokens
- Batch size target: 6 for latency-sensitive lane, 24 for throughput lane
- Warm-lane cache hit: 30% prefix reuse during peak (saw similar in PoC traffic)

Sizing notes: 
- 8 GPUs will support a conservative pilot for functional validation but will exhaust headroom at 95th for heavier prompts. Expect 15-20% increased latency during sustained peaks.
- 12 GPUs is the practical minimum to meet your stated latency SLO with an optimized batching policy and prefix caching.
- If you plan to run parallel heavy-ranking + multi-turn chat, budget for 1.5x the baseline (i.e., 18 GPUs) or use a separate lane for ranking.

Operational recommendations:
- Activation window: allow up to 6 hours to fully ramp new reserved instances (pre-warm + kernel warmup) if you scale committed pool mid-cycle.
- Keep a 10% burst credit pool for scheduled marketing/clinical events.

I'll add a short table to the worksheet with these assumptions. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your Eng Lead to map traffic curves.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Doe <caroline@sentinelhealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing + ramp cadence — pricing and terms

Caroline, Logan — following up with pricing buckets and contractual notes for the two options. Summary here and details in the attached worksheet: 

Pricing (indicative, list price ranges)
- Option 1 (Pilot-first): Effective rate ~ $18–22 / GPU-hour with pilot discounts and 30-day trial credits. Estimated monthly burn at 8 GPUs: $104k–$130k (depending on usage).
- Option 2 (12-month runway): Tiered commitments reduce unit cost to ~$12–15 / GPU-hour at scale. Estimated Month 12 steady-state burn at 36 GPUs: $310k–$390k / month.

Commercial guardrails and offer highlights:
- 60-day canary with rollback on quality regressions (we include model rollback + routing policies).
- 3 months of trial credits applied to first quarter if you commit to Phase A within 14 days.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime for committed capacity lanes, with credit-back calculation in the contract.
- Cancellation: 90-day notice after initial 6-month minimum for medium-term contracts; pilot contracts are month-to-month.

Attachments: I attached the workbook with line-item pricing and a sample term sheet we can use as the starting PO. If you want, we can pre-fill the PO with the Phase A numbers for quick sign-off.

Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dedicated-offer-worksheet.xlsx (updated), sentinel-term-sheet-draft.pdf (application/pdf)
